name: Can I convert a garage into a junior ADU instead of a full ADU?

mainEntity.name: When does a garage conversion make more sense as a junior ADU rather than a full accessory dwelling unit?
mainEntity.text: When does a garage conversion make more sense as a junior ADU rather than a full accessory dwelling unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: A junior ADU can be the better path when the goal is to create functional living space without taking on the full complexity of a separate dwelling unit. For some properties, that means a smaller footprint, simpler plumbing, and less extensive design work than a full ADU. It can also be a useful option when the owner wants extra flexibility for family use, a caregiver, or future housing needs without fully reworking the lot. The tradeoff is that a junior ADU may have more limitations than a full ADU in terms of independence, layout, and long-term rental strategy. Homeowners should compare the intended use carefully before selecting the classification. If the main objective is a private rental with maximum utility and privacy, a full ADU may be better. If the goal is lower cost and a more modest conversion, a junior ADU may be more efficient. The decision should be made early because it affects design, permit strategy, and utility planning.
acceptedAnswer.description: A junior ADU can make sense when the project needs to stay smaller, simpler, and more integrated with the main home. It often has a smaller scope than a full ADU and may be a better fit when the owner wants lower cost and less complexity.
